changes: Fixes the double-tap TRACK machine list on card builds with POLY8 beside VECTOR, FM Synth or Analog BD (#842, #941, #942): every machine now shows, UP and DOWN reach it, and YES picks it.
POLY8 alone, and POLY8 over USB, work as before.
Known issue: checked in the emulator only, not yet on a unit.
Fixes the Octatrack freezing while POLY8 plays (#646, likely #520). When the CPU runs short, POLY8 now drops voices: release tails first, then the oldest notes.
Fixes the sequencer and audio stopping until a power cycle with many held voices (likely #408).
Uses much less CPU on the beta base. The sound is unchanged.
How many voices play at once depends on your base: about three on the current beta base, more on others.
Known issue: not yet tested on the MKI, after reloading a project or after a power cycle.
POLY8 now installs beside Repitch and Mute Modes without being bundled with them.
Available over USB as its own package, beside every other module, on the Modwerk beta base.
Needs a recent Modwerk base; older bases refuse this version and keep 0.2.7-experimental.
Known issue: not yet tested on a unit.
Media only: new POLY8 thumbnail.
With HOLD INF, a finite AMP REL now lets the previous chord’s tails end when the next trig plays (#447). Notes played from the panel or MIDI are kept.
Finite HOLD, REL INF and STOP work as before. With HOLD INF, the last chord sustains until another trig or STOP; recorded key-up timing is not supported.
Known issue: the fix for #447 is not yet confirmed on the affected MKI.
POLY8 can now be combined with Repitch, Mute Modes and Scale Quantizer.
Adds a machine chooser for using POLY8, Analog BD, VECTOR and FM Synth together; each keeps its own saved Parts, controls and sound.
Fixes builds with other machines that could fail to boot or overwrite the other machine’s code.
Selecting POLY8 now stays on the current page, as with FLEX and STATIC; double-press TRACK for FLEX samples. NO closes the one-POLY8 message again.
Known issue: cannot be combined with Octakit; recording, loading and keeping settings over a restart are not yet fully tested.
First public experimental release as POLY8: eight shared sample voices, one POLY8 per Part, independent envelopes and fixed 1/8 gain.
Reselecting POLY8 keeps the track’s LOOP setting; newly assigned tracks still start with LOOP OFF.
LEFT from POLY8’s sample slots returns to the machine list; RIGHT opens FLEX samples again.
Uses less CPU; voices, envelopes and gain are unchanged.
Known issue: panel recording takes up to four notes within eleven semitones, length follows AMP HOLD, and MIDI recording and grid root editing are unfinished.
Test build: leaves the stock DSP code untouched to help find why POLY8 made no sound on an MKII.
Adds more diagnostic counters to the log.
Known issue: not a confirmed fix; recording, reboot, playback and audio are not yet tested with this version.
Test build: writes a diagnostic log to the card to help find the MKII stall.
Fixes a possible out-of-range memory access with many voices; not confirmed as the cause of the stall.
The one-POLY message now closes by itself after a short time, so it can no longer block the panel.
Known issue: the MKII recording and playback stalls stay open until this build is tested on hardware.
Allows one POLY track per Part; a second one is refused with a message you close with NO, before anything is changed.
Applies a fixed 1/8 (−18 dB) gain so eight full-level voices fit without the volume pumping as voices come and go.
Fixes POLY tracks being forgotten after a normal restart.
Known issue: the recording failure reported on the MKII is not fixed by this release.
Restores panel recording for chords of up to four notes within eleven semitones; sample locks still work.
Limits POLY to eight shared voices; released tails are taken before held notes, and pressing a held key again is ignored.
New POLY tracks start with LOOP OFF; existing LOOP settings are kept.
Known issue: recorded length follows AMP HOLD; wider chords, extended MIDI recording and grid root editing are not supported yet.
Adds 32 POLY voices in one shared pool; a single track can use all free voices.
Each voice has its own AMP envelope; filters and effects are shared per track.
PTCH tuning works independently of chromatic and MIDI notes, with ten panel octave positions and MIDI notes 0–127.
Selecting POLY opens FLEX samples directly; STATIC is not supported.
Known issue: hardware timing and note recording are not yet tested.
